suggestions: Insert a slow-moving filter on the rolling correlation before cross-sectional ranking, e.g. replace `Rank(Corr(...),20)` with `Rank(Ma(Corr(Ma(((close-low)/(high-low)),5),(Diff(volume,5)/Ma(volume,20)),20),10),20)`. Investment rationale: a 20-day correlation still reprices sharply as observations roll in and out of the window, so day-to-day rank reshuffling dominates portfolio changes even when the underlying accumulation story is unchanged; smoothing the correlation series targets the same persistent close-near-high plus rising-participation thesis while suppressing window-edge flicker that inflates turnover.

Replace the fast volume-change leg `Diff(volume,5)/Ma(volume,20)` with a slow participation slope such as `(Ma(volume,10)-Ma(volume,30))/Ma(volume,30)` (or `(Ma(volume,15)-Ma(volume,45))/Ma(volume,45)`). Investment rationale: a 5-day volume difference is still event-sensitive and re-anchors every session, which makes the price-volume correlation jump when liquidity spikes fade; comparing medium-term to longer-term average volume measures sustained participation shifts that evolve gradually, so the alpha should re-rank less often without weakening the volume-confirmation filter.

Rank-transform each input over a medium horizon before estimating correlation, e.g. `Corr(Rank(Ma(((close-low)/(high-low)),5),20), Rank((Diff(volume,5)/Ma(volume,20)),20), 30)` followed by the existing `Rank(...,20)` and `Zscore(...,60)`. Investment rationale: Pearson correlation on raw range-position and volume-trend levels overweights single-day microstructure extremes that are not durable buying pressure; correlating cross-sectional ranks emphasizes stable co-movement in relative standing rather than level spikes, producing a less volatile linkage estimate and therefore lower daily portfolio churn.
